result.title: Beyond feature attribution: Recovering latent interaction structures in machine learning models via localized CBFI
result.summary: Background: Understanding individual predictions in complex tabular models remains challenging, as existing additive frameworks like SHAP and LIME often obscure structural logic by absorbing nonlinear interactions into individual feature scores. Exposing these latent interaction structures is essential for automated auditing in high-stakes environments where understanding the logic of model behavior is as essential as predictive accuracy. Methods: To address this limitation, we introduce the localized case-based feature importance (CBFI) framework. Unlike traditional numerical attribution, our method decomposes instance-specific predictions into structurally distinct components, effectively separating independent main effects (G1) from pure interactions (G4) to capture explicit feature synergies and provide a principled approach for diagnosing feature combinations. Results: Comprehensive experiments on wine quality classification and medical insurance regression demonstrate that localized CBFI successfully disentangles complex interactions hidden by additive models. Furthermore, fidelity tests and synthetic ground-truth benchmarks confirm that the identified interactions correspond precisely to the nonlinear structural dependency patterns embedded in complex architectures, including gradient boosting and deep neural networks, thereby successfully shifting the explainable AI paradigm from simple numerical attribution to the recovery of interaction-driven contributions.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 localized CBFI 框架，将表格模型的单样本预测分解为主效应（G1）与纯交互项（G4），以恢复被 SHAP、LIME 等加性归因掩盖的潜在特征交互结构，并在合成真值与保真度测试上验证。
AI.relevance_reason: 其把预测分解为独立主效应与纯交互成分的思路，可能为 LVR 中 latent 状态、视觉证据与问题上下文之间「独立贡献 vs 协同贡献」的分配与诊断提供可核查的方法线索，但属纯表格 XAI，与视觉推理无直接联系。
